name: ASML Holding N.V. (ASML.AS, Euronext Amsterdam; all prices in EUR)
analyst_actions: 2026-09-16 | Bank of America Securities | reiterate Buy | EUR2452->EUR2452
2026-09-08 | Morgan Stanley | maintain Buy, PT cut | EUR1930->EUR1700
upcoming_dates: 2027-06-10 | investor day | Capital Markets Day, ASML to update longer-term views | https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/937966/000162828026048235/pressreleasefinancialresul.htm | primary
product: EUV including High-NA and DUV immersion lithography systems, metrology and inspection, computational lithography, plus Installed Base Management (service and field upgrades). More than 44,500 employees (FTE) as of July 2026.
demand: AI-driven Logic and Memory capex with customers accelerating capacity expansion. Q2 2026 net sales were EUR9.3bn and management described H1 2026 order intake as extremely strong, giving increasing visibility into longer-term demand.
pricing_power: Very strong in EUV and High-NA, where ASML is effectively a monopoly; High-NA tools cost about USD400m each. Group gross margin reached 54.0% in Q2 2026 with Q3 guided at 55-57%. Pricing power is strongest where no alternative exists.
competition: ASML holds a near-monopoly in EUV; Canon and Nikon compete only in DUV and have abandoned EUV. Emerging threats are Chinese domestic tools and alternative particle-accelerator lithography, both unproven, plus 3D integration approaches.
team: CEO Christophe Fouquet and CFO Roger Dassen lead; more than 44,500 employees (FTE). At the July 2026 results management expanded capacity and reaffirmed shareholder returns.
market_strategy: Extend Holistic Lithography across DUV, EUV and 3D integration; scale EUV capacity by 30% in 2027 and explore another 30% for 2028; deepen customer partnerships; return cash via growing dividend and buybacks; next Capital Markets Day on 2027-06-10.
bull: Q2 2026 (2026-07-15): sales EUR9.3bn, gross margin 54.0%, EPS EUR7.59; FY2026 outlook raised to EUR43-45bn at 54-56%; 2027 EUV and DUV immersion capacity +30%; H1 order intake called extremely strong.
bear: 2026-09-21 CXMT mass-produces advanced DRAM without ASML; 2026-09-08 CXMT/YMTC stockpiled ~3 years of DUV; 2026-09-16 AI-demand doubts, 7% one-day drop; Morgan Stanley cut PT 2026-09-08; forward P/E ~44x.
falsifier: Any ASML disclosure of 2026 order pushouts or cancellations, or a cut to the FY2026 EUR43-45bn sales / 54-56% margin outlook, on or before the 2027-06-10 Capital Markets Day.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 results on 2026-07-15: net sales EUR9.3bn, gross margin 54.0%, net income EUR2.9bn, EPS EUR7.59; FY2026 outlook raised to EUR43-45bn sales at 54-56% margin; 2027 low-NA EUV capacity +30% (from ~65) and DUV immersion +30% (from ~130); EUR1.88 interim dividend; EUR1.1bn buyback in Q2.
web_not_known_yesterday: 2026-09-24/25: the Dutch PM said he is confident of reaching a US deal on ASML China export curbs and raised it with Trump (Bloomberg, marketscreener). 2026-09-22: an ASML executive said the firm sold no chipmaking machines in Europe in 2026 (Bloomberg, NL Times).
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and demand led: AI-driven Logic and Memory capex; Q2 2026 net system sales EUR6.6bn on 86 new lithography systems; management called H1 2026 order intake extremely strong. Mix helps via High-NA and upgrades; gross-margin gains come from Installed Base Management and mix, not price inflation.
web_suppliers: Critical single-source suppliers: Carl Zeiss SMT (optics), TRUMPF (lasers) and in-house Cymer light sources, within ~5000 tier-1 suppliers. ASML flags supply-chain capacity and timely parts as risks and is expanding its own capacity. 2026-09-02 Bloomberg: an ASML supplier said China is about 15 years behind in top tools.
web_customers: Highly concentrated: TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK hynix and Micron dominate leading-edge EUV and High-NA demand. 2026-09-08 press releases: Intel Foundry runs High-NA in volume on select 18A layers (Panther Lake); Samsung plans High-NA in DRAM by 2028 and joined the 12-inch photomask initiative.
web_who_loses: Canon and Nikon lose the leading-edge lithography race since they compete only in DUV; Chinese fabs such as CXMT and YMTC are shut out by export controls. On 2026-09-18 ASML said it will not pursue particle-accelerator alternative lithography, a bet it loses if that tech matures.
web_contradicting_evidence: 2026-09-21: China CXMT began mass-producing advanced DRAM without ASML tools; 2026-09-08 reports said CXMT and YMTC stockpiled about three years of ASML DUV. 2026-09-16 fresh questions over future AI demand; a 7% one-day AI-fear drop; Morgan Stanley cut its target on 2026-09-08; forward P/E about 44x.
web_if_management_right: FY2026 sales of EUR43-45bn at 54-56% gross margin; 2027 capacity up 30% in both EUV and DUV immersion; High-NA moves into volume manufacturing (Intel 18A now, Samsung DRAM by 2028); order momentum persists and cash returns grow via dividend and buyback.
web_if_management_wrong: Order pushouts or cancellations and tighter China export controls hit system shipments first; customer capex cuts strand ASML's capacity build and rising R&D (about EUR1.3bn per quarter); gross margin and the buyback pace compress.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Optics, laser and mask supply chain: Carl Zeiss SMT, TRUMPF, mask makers and the new 12-inch photomask ecosystem; Dutch Brainport suppliers and contract manufacturers; metrology, inspection, EDA and computational-lithography partners riding ASML Holistic Litho adoption.
